name: llm-box
desc: Free, open-source local LLM server manager for Windows — llama.cpp presets, OpenAI-compatible API, VRAM fit checks. 100 MB portable, MIT.
features: ✅ **One-click server start** — pick a GGUF, auto-detect chat template, and get a running localhost endpoint in seconds
✅ **OpenAI-compatible API** — drop-in /v1/chat/completions on port 8080 that any app expects
✅ **VRAM fit check** — refuses to launch an obviously oversized offload without a clear warning and a suggested preset
✅ **Model switcher** — hot-swap loaded models from the tray without editing configs or restarting the app
✅ **Preset shelf** — context size, threads, GPU layers and batch size saved per model, portable across machines
✅ **Live log console** — token speed, context usage and errors streamed with filterable levels
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and server backend bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Free | Free, OSS |
| Runs raw GGUF from any folder | **Yes** | Import only | Yes | Yes |
| Tray model hot-swap | **Yes** | No | Partial | No |
| Per-model preset shelf | **Yes** | Modelfile | Yes | Config file |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Installer | Installer | Zip |
faqQ: how to run a local LLM server with an OpenAI-compatible API on Windows?
faqA: Most guides mean installing Python or a background service that registers itself and phones home. llm-box starts any GGUF you point it at, serves the /v1 API apps already expect and keeps every preset in a portable folder. It is a 100 MB exe, MIT, offline, and uninstalls by deleting a folder.
s1: Dark dashboard (#121417, green #34D399): model card with VRAM fit badge reading fits in 12.1 of 16 GB, start button glowing, endpoint chip localhost:8080/v1.

s3: Log console: chat completion streamed with 42 tok per sec counter, filter dropdown on requests, green toast reading server ready in 0.9 s.
